title: Minimum Operations to Maximize Last Elements in Arrays
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, determine the minimum number of operations required to make the last element of each array equal to the maximum value in its respective array.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, determine the minimum number of operations required to make the last element of each array equal to the maximum value in its respective array. An operation consists of swapping the values at the same index in both arrays. Return -1 if it's impossible to achieve the conditions.
constraints: Both positive-integer arrays have equal nonzero length.
One operation swaps values at the same index across arrays.
Minimize operations so each final last element is a maximum of its array, or return -1.
hints: Only two final-value orientations are possible: keep or swap the last pair.
For each orientation, every earlier pair is independently kept if it fits or swapped if that fits.
Count forced swaps, reject a pair fitting neither orientation, and include the last swap cost when applicable.
Once final bounds are fixed, choosing keep whenever possible is never worse; evaluating both exhaustive final orientations yields the global minimum.
editorial: Once final bounds are fixed, choosing keep whenever possible is never worse; evaluating both exhaustive final orientations yields the global minimum.

tests.explanation: Swapping the last pair makes final maxima three and seven in one operation.
Swap the last pair and index three to satisfy both arrays in two operations.
